## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (README: checks or gates run in digikit's emulator (not shipped)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz.

### analog-rytm-mkii-research

RE workspace for Rytm MKII OS 1.72: a custom QEMU ColdFire machine, a desktop emulator that boots your OS file, tracing scripts, audio-path notes. Licence: unspecified; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01)_

### Chopshop

Browser builder for Rytm MK1/MKII OS 1.73 (CHOP with step locks, sample focus, per-track cuts) and Analog Keys OS 1.56 (chord memory, joystick random). Not OS 1.74, not Analog Four. Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later; distribution: browser-installer. Listed by altstrument.

_Related: vendors `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: built on elektron-firmware-tool compiled to WebAssembly); builds on `rytm1-mods` (README: built on gdeo607's rytm1_mods) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### libanalogrytm

C library that decodes and encodes Rytm SysEx (kits, sounds, patterns, settings, projects); no MIDI I/O. Dormant since 2023. Licence: MIT; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01)_

### rytm-builder

Assembles Rytm project SysEx from a library of pattern/kit dumps (Rust CLI and a Mac app); does not send MIDI. OS 1.70 object layout. Licence: MIT; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01)_

### rytm-fw-re

RE notes for Rytm MKII OS 1.74 (container, boot, display) and a tiny from-source replacement OS that boots on a unit, plus same-size splash and LED-palette patches. Recovery only over DIN MIDI. Licence: unspecified; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument.

_Related: uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: it unpacks and repacks the OS) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### rytm-mods-src

Public copy of MrScruff's Rytm MKII OS 1.73 mods (euclid accents, velocity humanise, random LFO, kit A/B, slice loop, control-all and more). Licence: GPL-2.0-only; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument. Also reachable as connorway32/rytm-mods-src (same HEAD 3a98e23, 2026-11-03). 2026-11-08: 0017 lets a CTRL IN jack in CV or EXPR mode drive one of the performance macros PF1-PF12 (device-wide setting); 0018 lets a scene store track mutes (SCENE held, FUNC + trig), kept per kit in the project. Its re/subsystems notes (control inputs, scenes and mutes, the "loosened" kit and sound bytes) are folded into hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md.

_Related: uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: fetched and built into vendor/ by setup, not shipped); mod for `modwerk` (modwerk sdk/analog-rytm-mkii/modules ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes name mods/0017-ctrl-in-perf and mods/0018-scene-mutes of this repo as source) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### Sidecar | Expander

A Raspberry Pi 4B/5 on the Rytm's USB port adds digital voices, effects and a sequencer; the Rytm runs a patched OS. 0.3.2 adds experimental, emulator-only Digitakt support. The Teensy variant is frozen. GPL-2.0. On 2026-11-09, Analog Four MKII support since 0.4.0 (A4 firmware a4-v0.12, OS 1.56); 0.4.3 caps the Rytm screen redraws after users saw a sluggish Rytm at 20-40 redraws a second. 2026-11-13: a card config editor on the documentation site writes the Pi's config.txt and cmdline.txt in the browser. 2026-11-15 (INSTALL-PI): from Sidecar 0.5.0 a release is to ship a starter zip that fills one FAT32 card with the boot files, a new web app (in a hidden folder), every user machine and effect, starter content and demo samples; without the web-app folder the Pi serves the classic page. 2026-11-16 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.0, KNOWN-ISSUES, docs): 0.5.0 drops the OS 1.73 build; the Pi 5 is now the recommended board (2 GB minimum, 4 GB recommended); MORPH, the looper and sidechain moved to 0.5.1. The 0.5.0 features are marked in testing on their pages. The voices clipped at the stock Rytm's track ceiling in 0.4.x and now play 9 dB lower. Do not combine with newer elekloader cores: they store their settings in the bytes Sidecar uses.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: the Rytm firmware part is an elekloader module); uses tool `analog-emu` (README: built or checked in trigcondition/analog-emu) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-02, README, README (2026-11-11), README, INSTALL-PI (2026-11-15), README, RELEASE-NOTES, docs (2026-11-16)_

### ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)

Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

### ElekPrep Transfer

Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03)_

### Elektron Project Companion

Windows editor for arranging live sets from local project backups: place patterns in banks A-H and export a new project for Transfer. Rytm MKII: .arprj and whole-project .syx (patterns, kits, sound locks, sample references). Digitakt II: .dt2prj project image v4 (patterns with their kits; merging only with identical sample pools, since relocating a sample changes locks). File-level testing on a real OS. Licence not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-07, README_

### Sidecar | Expander: Rytm mods

The source of the Analog Rytm MKII OS mods that Sidecar | Expander needs: patch sources, symbol map, allocation registry and the build that turns the user's own stock .syx into a modded one, as one elekloader module per OS; the Analog Four MKII's mod in a4/. 0.4.0 reports each track's pan and route (stereo through mode), adds MD's own page, preset browsers for JUNO and 6-OP FM, DSP SAMPLE's sample picker, list knobs of up to 36 names, a MIDI machine (machine 50) and arpeggiator settings in the sound. Sidecar Mini (Teensy) is frozen at 0.1.0. 2026-11-16 (v0.5.0): SAMPLER as machine 43, the Rytm's own sound parameters moved from the Pi (an offset or override added in the audio interrupt, never written to the kit), UP + RIGHT for FILL, a browser preview and file menu, send effect BASE/WIDTH. It needs elekloader core 0.1: newer cores keep their settings in the same bytes and the set is refused as an overlap. A mod SysEx report sent between the parts of a stock pattern dump cut the dump; fixed in 0.5.0 (I111).

_Related: same project `sidecar-expander` (README: the Rytm mods that Sidecar | Expander uses); mod for `elekloader` (README: one elekloader module per OS) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README, README (2026-11-11), README, ELEKLOADER.md, design notes, re/os (v0.5.0, 2026-11-16)_

### elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)

One local MCP server per PC that gives AI agent sessions the same tools for testing Elektron units (Analog Rytm MKII, Analog Four MKII, Digitone; Digitakt untested on hardware) and their emulators: claim a unit, run a test plan, flash an OS, take screenshots, record and check USB audio, take or restore an Overbridge Total Recall image. It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same. 2026-11-11 (config example): an optional emulator headroom check waits for CPU, free RAM and a cap on running emulators before each emulator start. 2026-11-12: emulator timing (analog-emu unit or exact timing, the Sidecar's Overbridge stream on the Rytm) and a CPU gate that fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU. 2026-11-13: elklock marks a unit that stalled on its restart after a flash and refuses every device command on it until a watched power cycle (elkflash usb-cycle). 2026-11-14: DIN MIDI interfaces are configured per interface, not per unit; at a run's first DIN step elkbench probes each interface with the unit's working-kit dump request and uses the one that answers, so a cable can move between units without a config change; elklock locks each interface as its own device.

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: emulator first; sidecar-emu reaches analog-emu through it) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README, README, config.example.toml (2026-11-14)_

### sidecar-emu (Sidecar emulator)

QEMU cut down to the Raspberry Pi 4B and the devices Sidecar's engine needs: boots the Sidecar engine image, answers over Ethernet, puts an Analog Rytm MKII stand-in on its USB-A side and gives its USB-C gadget a raw MIDI TCP port, so an OS upgrade or an elkbench run can go through the emulated Pi into analog-emu. A local experiment, not meant for QEMU upstream.

### trig-seedr

Offline pattern algorithms as an elekloader mod, opened as a third TRIG page after EUCLIDEAN: generate rhythms, notes, accents, trig conditions, retrigs and sample locks for a track, audition takes with undo, apply groove timing and velocity, and rotate a track or the whole pattern. Everything it writes is ordinary pattern data that plays and saves on a stock OS. Analog Four MKII and Syntakt are planned. Groove tables can be made from the user's own Ableton Live grooves; none are shipped. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README and firmware notes read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-16 (v0.4.0/v0.4.1, README 0.5): navigation is LEFT/RIGHT, PAGE and the TRIG keys stay stock's while the page is open. 0.4.1 is the build to flash: 0.4.0 wrote new trigs without the stock SYN/SMP/ENV flag bits, and a compiler optimisation (store merging in m68k-elf-gcc 16.2) broke a step move in the emulator (I112). Recipes live in RAM only and are lost at power-off or a pattern change. The MAP source copies Grids' drum map (GPL-3.0, Mutable Instruments, not catalogued).

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: an elekloader mod on core-ar2 0.13); uses tool `analog-emu` (README: tested in trigcondition/analog-emu); cites `libanalogrytm` (firmware notes: pattern.h as a source) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_
